title: Patient name and address records
prompt: The patient portal stores names and addresses as nested records. Write `solve(patients)` so each patient comes back with a `name` struct and an `address` struct.
rules: `name` has the fields `first` and `last`, from `first_name` and `last_name`, in that order.
`address` has the fields `city`, `state` and `zip` (from `postal_code`), in that order. Postal codes stay text, leading zeros included.
Every patient gets both structs, even when some or all of the values inside are missing.
hints: `F.struct(...)` builds one struct column from several columns.
Each field takes its column's name unless you rename it with `alias` inside `F.struct`.
Name the whole struct with one more `alias` outside: `F.struct(F.col("first_name").alias("first"), ...).alias("name")`.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(patients):
    # Return patient_id, a name struct and an address struct.
    return patients
explanation: Build each struct with `F.struct`, renaming the fields inside and the struct outside: `F.struct(F.col("first_name").alias("first"), F.col("last_name").alias("last")).alias("name")` and `F.struct("city", "state", F.col("postal_code").alias("zip")).alias("address")`. Fields come out in the order you list them, and `F.struct` always builds a struct, so a patient with no address details still gets one whose fields are all missing. `postal_code` is text, so leave it as it is; casting it to a number would lose leading zeros.
